# Identity and sign-in

Keycloak signs people in with passkeys or hardware security keys only; there are no passwords. Its settings are applied from the repository as code, and its data sits in a PostgreSQL database we build ourselves. oauth2-proxy sits in front of each workbench session, so a session is reached only after sign-in.

## image:docker.io/adorsys/keycloak-config-cli

**What it provides.** keycloak-config-cli 6.5.1: applies the site realm as code at install and on every update, as a Kubernetes Job (Decision 10).

**Why it is needed.** Applies the site's sign-in settings (flows, clients and policies) from the repository at install and on every update, as a one-off Job. The settings are reviewed like code and cannot drift through hand changes.

| Licence | Apache-2.0 |
| Cryptography | Not a validated cryptographic module |
| Air gap | Works air-gapped once mirrored: the pinned digest in the site registry, carried with its signature by the offline bundle |
| Compliance fit | Pass with conditions |
| Controls | IA-2, IA-5, IA-8, AC-12, AU-2, AU-3, SC-13, SC-23 |
| Security fixes | Re-pinned by hand in a reviewed change when upstream publishes a fixed release (watch the project's security advisories). No scan of this third-party image runs in CI yet; Phase 48 adds a scan of the bundle's images. |
| Reviewed | Claude (agent review; owner to confirm), 2026-11-24 |

Conditions:

- CVE-2026-6856: the fixed version is unverified. The 26.8.2 source refuses self-attestation and the none attestation when an AAGUID allowlist is set; Phase 48 closes this (D-30).
- Owner to confirm (E6): FIPS strict mode with BC-FIPS is not delivered in Phase 47.
- Password, OTP and recovery-code authenticators are off in every flow; Keycloak events are shipped to the site log store.
- Holds a Keycloak admin credential only for the Job's run and opens no inbound port.
- The upstream image is a JVM image not built on UBI 9 and carries no validated cryptographic module: it is conditional at Protected B (SC-13) until it is rebuilt on UBI 9 with the OpenSSL FIPS provider on a FIPS-mode host, or your organization's authorizing official accepts it.

## image:quay.io/keycloak/keycloak

**What it provides.** Keycloak 26.8.2: passkey sign-in for the site (D-30), on the official ubi9-micro image.

**Why it is needed.** Signs people in at the site with passkeys or hardware security keys only, with no passwords. The session sign-in proxy and the parts behind it trust the identity Keycloak issues. Without it each part would need its own sign-in.

## image:registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/go-toolset

**What it provides.** Build stage of our oauth2-proxy image: compiles it from pinned source with the Go FIPS module (Go 1.27.3).

**Why it is needed.** Compiles our own oauth2-proxy from pinned source with the Go FIPS module. Building it ourselves, instead of using the upstream image, is what puts the session sign-in proxy on a UBI 9 base. Build stage only: just the compiled program reaches the final image.

| Compliance fit | Pass with conditions |

| Security fixes | The rebuilt image is scanned by grype (report-only, --only-fixed --fail-on high) in deploy-images on every PR that changes it; the base digest is re-pinned by hand in a reviewed change when Red Hat publishes a fixed image. |
| Reviewed | Claude (agent review; owner to confirm), 2026-11-24 |

Conditions:

- Rebuilt from pinned source with the Go FIPS module (GOFIPS140); the module's CMVP status is unverified.

- Build stage only: nothing but the compiled binary reaches the final image.

## image:registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/ubi-minimal

**What it provides.** Runtime base of our oauth2-proxy and Postgres images, and the build and runtime base of the Sterling workbench image (Node 26 binary copied in, native addons built on it).

**Why it is needed.** The small Red Hat UBI 9 base of our oauth2-proxy and PostgreSQL images and of the Sterling workbench image. UBI 9 carries the RHEL OpenSSL FIPS provider, the base the hosting design asks for at Protected B on a host in FIPS mode. *This role is waiting for the owner to confirm it.*

- Rebuilt from pinned source with the Go FIPS module (GOFIPS140); the module's CMVP status is unverified.

- Built only into images this repository rebuilds (deploy/images, D-23): each is signed with your organization's one cosign key in the container-release environment, with a CycloneDX SBOM and an attestation; no keyless signing.
- Workbench: mirror the pinned digest in a local registry through the builder's registry-mirror setting (D-39); FIPS mode is a host property (Phase 47); swap to Red Hat's Node 26 minimal image when it is published.

## chart:keycloakx

**What it provides.** codecentric keycloakx Helm chart 7.4.0, rendered with the official Keycloak 26.8.2 image (Decision 10).

**Why it is needed.** Installs Keycloak, with the official Keycloak image at the site from the vendored, hash-checked chart tarball, with our settings. Its images come from the pinned image lock. Without the chart we would write and maintain the Kubernetes manifests ourselves.

## tool:postgresql

**What it provides.** PostgreSQL 18.7 RPMs from PGDG with their signing key, installed into our Postgres image for Keycloak (Decision 2, spike S3).

**Why it is needed.** Keycloak's database: user records and passkey public credentials, kept across restarts. We build it ourselves on UBI 9 from signed packages. Keycloak cannot keep its users without a database.
